levelNote: Foundational questions on Charles II, theatres, Dryden, Congreve, Behn, Milton, Bunyan and Pepys.

questions.question: In which year was Charles II restored to the English throne?
questions.explanation: Charles II returned in May 1660 after the Interregnum, restoring the Stuart monarchy.

questions.question: On what date did Charles II make his ceremonial return to London?
questions.explanation: Charles II entered London on 29 May 1660, the day of his thirtieth birthday.

questions.question: Which king was the father of the monarch restored in 1660?
questions.explanation: Charles I was executed in 1649; his son Charles II regained the throne in 1660.

questions.question: Who succeeded Charles II as monarch in 1685?
questions.explanation: Charles II died in February 1685, and his brother James, Duke of York, succeeded him.

questions.question: Which document issued in April 1660 helped prepare the return of Charles II?
questions.explanation: The Declaration of Breda promised pardons and qualified freedom of conscience.

questions.question: Which English city suffered the Great Fire of 1666 during the Restoration?
questions.explanation: The Great Fire of September 1666 destroyed much of central London.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the reign of Charles II:
I. He returned to the English throne in 1660.
II. The Great Fire of London occurred during his reign.
III. He was succeeded immediately by his father Charles I.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Charles II returned in 1660 and ruled during the fire of 1666. His brother James II succeeded him in 1685.

questions.question: What happened to the public theatres after Charles II returned in 1660?
questions.explanation: Charles II authorized companies to stage public plays, reversing the long closure.

questions.question: Who managed the King’s Company after the reopening of the theatres?
questions.explanation: Killigrew held the royal patent for the King’s Company.

questions.question: Which playwright led the Duke’s Company under royal patronage?
questions.explanation: Davenant managed the Duke’s Company, sponsored by the Duke of York.

questions.question: Who began performing female roles professionally on the English public stage after 1660?
questions.explanation: Professional actresses became a defining feature of Restoration performance.

questions.question: Which work did William Davenant present as a musical entertainment in 1656?
questions.explanation: Davenant’s The Siege of Rhodes was staged during the theatre restrictions.

questions.question: Who wrote the Restoration comedy The Way of the World?
questions.explanation: Congreve’s The Way of the World is a leading comedy of manners.

questions.question: In which year was The Way of the World first performed?
questions.explanation: The Way of the World appeared on the London stage in 1700.

questions.question: Which woman is Mirabell’s witty partner in The Way of the World?
questions.explanation: Millamant and Mirabell negotiate marriage as partners in wit.

questions.question: Which male character courts Millamant in The Way of the World?
questions.explanation: Mirabell and Millamant are the play’s central lovers.

questions.question: Which play was Congreve’s first major theatrical success in 1693?
questions.explanation: The Old Bachelor established Congreve as a successful young dramatist in 1693.

questions.question: Who wrote the comedy The Rover?
questions.explanation: Aphra Behn wrote The Rover, a Restoration comedy staged in 1677.

questions.question: In which year was Aphra Behn’s The Rover first performed?
questions.explanation: The Rover was staged in 1677 and became her best-known comedy.

questions.question: Which prose work by Aphra Behn follows an African prince enslaved in Surinam?
questions.explanation: Oroonoko depicts an enslaved African prince and his resistance to oppression.

questions.question: Which playwright is often described as an early English woman who earned her living by writing?
questions.explanation: Behn wrote plays and prose for income and helped establish professional female authorship.

questions.question: Which play was Aphra Behn’s first staged work, performed in 1670?
questions.explanation: The Forc’d Marriage was staged in September 1670.

questions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Professional actresses appeared on the English public stage after the Restoration.
Statement II: The royal patents of 1660 established two licensed theatrical companies.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:
options: Statement I is false, but Statement II is true
Statement I is true, but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.explanation: The reopened theatres featured professional actresses and operated under two royal patents.

questions.question:
Arrange the following events in the correct chronological order:
1. First performance of The Way of the World.
2. First performance of Love for Love.
3. First performance of The Old Bachelor.
4. Restoration of Charles II.
Choose the correct sequence:
questions.explanation: Charles II returned in 1660, followed by The Old Bachelor in 1693, Love for Love in 1695 and The Way of the World in 1700.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Aphra Behn:
I. The Rover was staged in 1677.
II. Oroonoko concerns an African prince who is enslaved.
III. Behn wrote The Way of the World.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Behn wrote The Rover and Oroonoko. The Way of the World was written by William Congreve.

questions.question: Who became Poet Laureate in 1668?
questions.explanation: Dryden was appointed Poet Laureate in 1668 during the reign of Charles II.

questions.question: Which poet wrote Astraea Redux to welcome the returning monarch in 1660?
questions.explanation: Dryden’s Astraea Redux celebrates the return of Charles II.

questions.question: Which poem by Dryden uses biblical characters to satirize the Exclusion Crisis?
questions.explanation: Absalom and Achitophel (1681) reshapes contemporary political conflict as biblical allegory.

questions.question: Which writer is ridiculed as the heir to dullness in Dryden’s MacFlecknoe?
questions.explanation: Dryden’s mock-heroic satire presents Shadwell as the successor of Flecknoe.

questions.question: Which Dryden tragedy retells the story of Antony and Cleopatra?
questions.explanation: All for Love (1677) reworks the lovers’ tragic story in blank verse.

questions.question: In which year did Paradise Lost first appear in print?
questions.explanation: Milton’s epic Paradise Lost was first published in 1667.

questions.question: Which biblical pair is central to the Fall described in Paradise Lost?
questions.explanation: The epic narrates the temptation and fall of Adam and Eve.

questions.question: Which kind of verse is used in Paradise Lost?
questions.explanation: Milton composed the epic in unrhymed iambic pentameter.

questions.question: Which shorter epic did Milton publish alongside Samson Agonistes in 1671?
questions.explanation: Paradise Regained and Samson Agonistes appeared together in 1671.

questions.question: Which Milton work dramatizes a hero from the Book of Judges?
questions.explanation: Samson Agonistes presents the biblical hero’s final struggle in dramatic form.

questions.question: Which poet of the Restoration had become blind before completing his great epic?
questions.explanation: Milton was blind when he completed and published Paradise Lost.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about John Dryden:
I. He wrote Astraea Redux in 1660.
II. He was appointed Poet Laureate in 1668.
III. He wrote The Pilgrim’s Progress.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Dryden welcomed the returning king in Astraea Redux and became Poet Laureate in 1668. Bunyan wrote The Pilgrim’s Progress.

questions.question: Who wrote The Pilgrim’s Progress?
questions.explanation: Bunyan’s allegorical narrative follows Christian on a spiritual journey.

questions.question: What is the name of the central pilgrim in Part I of The Pilgrim’s Progress?
questions.explanation: Christian journeys from destruction toward salvation.

questions.question: From which place does Christian begin his journey in The Pilgrim’s Progress?
questions.explanation: Christian leaves the City of Destruction at the start of his pilgrimage.

questions.question: What is the destination of Christian’s pilgrimage?
questions.explanation: The Heavenly City represents the goal of Christian’s spiritual journey.

questions.question: Which writer kept a famous diary during the early Restoration?
questions.explanation: Pepys recorded everyday life, politics and disasters during the reign of Charles II.

questions.question: What years are covered by Samuel Pepys’s celebrated diary?
questions.explanation: Pepys kept his extensive diary from January 1660 until 1669.

questions.question: Which institution employed Samuel Pepys during the Restoration?
questions.explanation: Pepys was a naval administrator and recorded his work in the Navy Office.

questions.question: Which disaster of 1666 did Pepys describe as an eyewitness?
questions.explanation: Pepys witnessed and described the Great Fire in his diary.

questions.question: In what year was Pepys’s diary first published?
questions.explanation: His diary was written in shorthand and first printed in 1825.

questions.question: Which genre satirizes fashionable society through witty dialogue and courtship intrigue?
questions.explanation: Comedy of manners exposes social pretension, flirtation and hypocrisy.

questions.question: Which Restoration dramatic form commonly features grand heroes torn between love and honour?
questions.explanation: Heroic drama favoured elevated action and a conflict between love and honour.

questions.question: Which verse form is closely associated with Dryden’s satire and criticism?
questions.explanation: A heroic couplet consists of two rhyming iambic-pentameter lines.

questions.question: What literary form describes characters and places standing for abstract ideas in Bunyan’s narrative?
questions.explanation: In allegory, story elements represent moral or spiritual meanings beyond the literal action.
